In the wake of this loss, the media is going to question whether it was a good idea to start the rookie quarterback. To me, that's like asking if it was a good idea for Thomas Edison to invent the light bulb. Yes, the rookie is a rookie (or after today, WAS a rookie) with no playoff experience, but if he's your franchise quarterback for 2017 and beyond, you need to get him acclimated to a playoff atmosphere at some point, especially if you're planning on a multi-year championship window. Otherwise, you're just shooting yourself in the foot for the next time you make the playoffs!

I know there are no moral victories in football, but there is gain to be had beyond the 2016 season. Next time the rookie leads the team to the playoffs, he'll be older, wiser, and more experienced. Call me crazy, but the second the veteran starter went down, any thoughts of instant gratification became a fool's errand. The second the veteran starter went down, I lost all faith that he could establish the team as a dominant force within the conference. The second the veteran starter went down, the plan was survival, and nothing else.

But the rookie saved the team from the zombie apocalypse that was the conference, teeming with the likes of the Seahawks, the Packers, the Cardinals and the Panthers (well, those last two regressed horribly, but they were still credible threats when the veteran starter went down). The rookie didn't help you survive.

He helped you thrive.

He helped you conquer.

He helped you reach the safe haven that we call the NFL Postseason.

And though you ultimately didn't get to savor the fruits of victory, you became all the stronger for it, maybe strong enough to finally reach that promised land with the wisdom the rookie has gained all throughout this season. And that is why I will never take seriously anyone who says the veteran starter should have started over the rookie.
